concerns.concern: Bmab is excluded near the transition onset mainly because the monoclinic B21/a model fits better. That model has more free parameters and twin fractions, and the monoclinic angle deviation is called negligible, so no statistical test or β uncertainty shows the difference is significant.
concerns.quote: the fit to the data employing monoclinic symmetry B21/a compared to orthorhombic Bmab is much better as shown in Table S4

concerns.concern: The DFT claim that no intermediate phase exists is called unequivocal, yet the relaxed phase depended on the starting structure. No enthalpies of independently relaxed candidate phases are compared, and the 1 mHa energy convergence is likely coarser than the relevant energy differences.
concerns.quote: the relaxation could have stopped in the tetragonal (or even in one of the orthorhombic) at low pressure... depending on the starting crystal structure.

concerns.concern: Extra Raman modes do not prove point-symmetry lowering below 2/m. A density-wave supercell that keeps a 2/m space group would also fold in additional modes, so the 'below 2/m' and Pc/P21 conclusions are not justified.
concerns.quote: The emergence of these extra Raman-active modes signifies that DW-driven lattice distortions induce a breaking of monoclinic P21/c symmetry.

concerns.concern: The centering-violating reflections attributed to twinning would also appear for a twinned Bmab phase. They show symmetry breaking below tetragonal but cannot distinguish monoclinic from orthorhombic, so they should not be presented as evidence against Bmab.
concerns.quote: it manifests from the microscopic domains of the single crystal induced by the phase transition, similar to the more recent work by Li, et al.

concerns.concern: No group-theoretical (Landau/symmetry-mode) analysis supports a direct continuous I4/mmm→P21/c transition. Such a transition is non-generic and would typically be first-order or go through intermediate phases.
concerns.quote: as the transition from 4/mmm to 2/m is continuous bypassing the orthorhombic phase due to the lack of orthogonality of β

concerns.concern: The transition is described both as weak first-order (a jump in β) and as continuous, and is fitted with mean-field laws. These descriptions are inconsistent.
concerns.quote: a jump in the value of β at the onset of the 2/m phase, which could be attributed to a weak first-order phase transition

concerns.concern: The DFT critical pressure 16.47 ± 0.04 GPa comes from three-point fits with a fixed exponent on a roughly 1 GPa grid. This overstates the precision and cannot exclude an intermediate phase narrower than the sampling.
concerns.quote: the three order parameters all nullify at the same critical pressure found to be Pc = 16.47 ± 0.04 GPa.

concerns.concern: The Raman polarization selection rules do not cleanly separate Ag and Bg modes when the in-plane polarizations are not aligned with crystal axes and several twin domains lie under the laser spot. Modes can leak between geometries, undermining the per-geometry counts.
concerns.quote: while the polarization Y and Z are in the (bc) plane but not aligned with a particular axis

concerns.concern: The non-detection of density-wave satellites in XRD has no quantitative detection limit. Readers cannot tell whether it contradicts Zhang et al. or is merely less sensitive.
concerns.quote: No discernible structural distortions associated with DW ordering are detected down to 20 K at ambient pressure.

concerns.concern: The claim of measurements down to 20 K at ambient pressure does not match the methods. These describe ambient-pressure refinements only at 230 and 80 K, while the 20 K data are under pressure.
concerns.quote: The 'down to 20 K at ambient pressure' statement is not matched by the described ambient-pressure data sets.

concerns.concern: The DFT methods do not state spin polarization, magnetic configuration, use of +U, or smearing. These choices can shift the critical pressure and the relative stability of tilt patterns, so the calculations are not reproducible.
concerns.quote: the magnetic state is unspecified

concerns.concern: The DFT stress convergence threshold is quoted in force units (Ha/Bohr), so the stress criterion is undefined.
concerns.quote: stresses have different units, so the stress threshold is undefined

concerns.concern: Ruling out P-1 with 51 modes against a limit of 48 is a thin margin. It requires the modes from the two geometries to be distinct and no spurious features to be counted, so 'certainly' is too strong.
concerns.quote: Since we measure a total of 51 phonon modes at low temperature, we can certainly rule out P¯1 as the low temperature space group.

concerns.concern: The pressure error estimate (3 GPa for a 1% change of b) appears inconsistent with the measured compressibility and bulk modulus, which imply about 5–8 GPa. It is used to claim agreement between the DFT and experimental Pc.
concerns.quote: If we estimate the error on pressure as the value here required to shrink the b parameter by 1%, we will get ∆P = 3 GPa.

concerns.concern: Reporting both q1 and q2 superlattice wavevectors plus mixed-order combinations would imply a 2-k, 4-fold cell in a single domain. This contradicts the stated 2-fold superstructure unless the text says they come from different twin domains.
concerns.quote: along with mixed-order satellite reflections corresponding to linear combinations

concerns.concern: The conclusion that superconductivity emerges only in the tetragonal phase is overstated. No transport or magnetic measurements were performed, so the work only shows a structural boundary consistent with the literature.
concerns.quote: This affirms that superconductivity emerges only once the system is restored to the tetragonal phase under pressure.

concerns.concern: The oxygen content is not reported even though EPMA used an oxygen standard. Oxygen stoichiometry is relevant to the discrepancies the authors attribute to sample quality.
concerns.quote: Both techniques confirm the La:Ni 4:3 atomic ratio.

concerns.concern: Secondary phases (NiO, La2NiO4) and possible Ruddlesden–Popper intergrowths are not excluded as sources of the new low-temperature Raman features.
concerns.quote: La2NiO4 has its own low-temperature structural transition. Its possible contribution to Raman features emerging at low temperature is not addressed.

concerns.concern: A single equation of state is fitted across the structural transition. The large temperature variation of the bulk modulus is not discussed, and whether K′ was fixed is not stated.
The Raman figure caption says the Poynting vector is perpendicular to X, contradicting the Porto notation and main text, which place it along X.
concerns.quote: the caption says 'The Poynting vector is perpendicular to X'

concerns.concern: The quoted mode counts for Pc/P21 include the three acoustic modes; the optical counts should be given instead.
concerns.quote: the 51 A + 51 B quoted for Pc/P21 include the three acoustic modes

concerns.concern: Calling the B21/a cell 'primitive' is self-contradictory because B21/a is a B-centered setting. It is unclear which cell β refers to.
concerns.quote: β is the angle between the a and c vectors of the primitive cell in the B21/a setting

concerns.concern: The density-wave transition temperature is given inconsistently (135 K, 130 K, ~120 K, 120–150 K) across the paper.
concerns.quote: T_DW is given as ≈135 K (abstract), ≈130 K (introduction, Fig. 6), and ~120 K or 120–150 K (Raman text).
